Both candidates currently have BPR set to 0.0 bar, which is a critical safety failure; the BPR must be raised to at least 1.8 bar (recommended 2.5 bar) to contain the vapor pressure of acetic acid at 80°C plus system backpressure. Material compatibility is acceptable with PFA, as it resists hot acetic acid, whereas FEP would be risky at this temperature. Hazard flags include corrosivity and potential inhalation risks from acetic acid vapors, requiring closed-system handling and proper venting. Atmosphere isolation is not required as the process is single-stage and O2-insensitive.
